pr_title: Add temperature to the light color mode parameter fallbacks
pr_body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!
  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).
-->

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
Some warm/cold white lights only understand the `color_temp` parameter, and as highlighted in #45111 the [color profiles](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/3bb9be23820c94dba75db1001878f06c81800db6/homeassistant/components/light/light_profiles.csv) only send XY values.

This PR indirectly solves that issue by adding an additional color temperature fallback mode when computing alternative color formats that are supported by the device: if it must resort to the color temperature attribute, it is now computed from the original XY values instead of ignored.

This incidentally enables devices like the IKEA Tradfri white-only bulbs to be controlled by specifying any color format and having it automatically converted instead of needing to manually specify a color temperature.

#### Future-proofing?

Abiding to #79591 the main attribute being set is `ATTR_COLOR_TEMP_KELVIN`, but given that some devices still need `ATTR_COLOR_TEMP` and the conversion would happen _before_ the rest of the color mode fallback code runs ([`preprocess_turn_on_alternatives`](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/6a89b3a135ebaff1f3c8f6dbc8e32974241b5e8f/homeassistant/components/light/__init__.py#L295) runs [before](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/6a89b3a135ebaff1f3c8f6dbc8e32974241b5e8f/homeassistant/components/light/__init__.py#L430) the actual [fallback conversions](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/6a89b3a135ebaff1f3c8f6dbc8e32974241b5e8f/homeassistant/components/light/__init__.py#L470)), at the moment I've resorted to manually deriving and applying the `ATTR_COLOR_TEMP` attribute (see commit [007e863](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/commit/007e86384a62e5def1a2b91cf93ee6f276ad7450)) once again.

This approach would rely on manually reaping any occurrence of `ATTR_COLOR_TEMP` when getting rid of it in the future, so I don't particularly like it. What could be a cleaner solution? Is there even a real need for it or is the one implemented here good enough already? Calling `preprocess_turn_on_alternatives` after the conversion would be counterintuitive but something of that sort would be needed in order to re-parse the Kelvin value and automatically fill in the legacy Mired one.

## Additional information
<!--

  Please be sure to fill out additional details, if applicable.
-->

- This PR fixes or closes issue: fixes #45111 
- The XY to Temperature conversion code uses [McCamy's approximation](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/col.5080170211) of the CCT curve, considered to be reliable for ranges between 2000 K and 10_000 K, thus enough for this use case. More accurate but also more complex models exist.

@nmaggioni I don't understand the reason for this change. Why would anyone want to set a light which only supports white to a color; the light will anyway just be white and it will be very tricky for the user to work out which part of the color space can be rendered by the light?

If the real driver is to improve light profiles, light profiles should be improved instead. Light profiles are very long overdue for an overhaul; we should either remove light profiles altogether and rely on scenes or modernize them with UI support and so on.

> I don't understand the reason for this change. Why would anyone want to set a light which only supports white to a color;

The linked issue should contain sufficient justification :)
As of today, applying a `profile` to bulbs that only support `color_temperature` simply changes their brightness. 

> the light will anyway just be white and it will be very tricky for the user to work out which part of the color space can be rendered by the light?

This PR only adds internal color conversion utilities to automatically translate a requested state into one that the final device will actually understand and act on: the UI certainly won't expose full color controls, so if a user wants to go in there and manually tinker with the services' payloads nobody will be surprised when the bulb won't react to "impossible" states (just like it does without these changes, honestly). Also you can't say that the actual behavior of requesting a color/temperature change and seeing only a brightness response is any better.

The only actual behavioral change this code brings is that HA's default color presets will work as expected in terms of temperature, so users of temperature-only bulbs won't need to implement custom profiles and/or dedicated automations to replicate the states that are built into the stock apps for, let's say, my IKEA Tradfri bulbs that come with three temperature settings that can be toggled by the stock remote.

Since [you contributed code related to this exact matter](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/commit/5f2326fb5756b85255cec27d3b2172c44bc66058) I'm surprised by your criticism, as this PR is basically just an extra `elif` that wasn't implemented at the time due to, I guess, simply not having encountered these somewhat weird bulbs.

> If the real driver is to improve light profiles, light profiles should be improved instead. Light profiles are very long overdue for an overhaul; we should either remove light profiles altogether and rely on scenes or modernize them with UI support and so on.

I'm totally with you on this one, but back in January this was the biggest contribution I could make and it worked pretty well for me for quite a long time. I don't really care if this gets merged or profiles get improved: the goal here is to make light profiles work with all bulbs. The difference between the two alternatives is that this PR will immediately fix the issue, while I'm not aware of any ongoing effort to improve or replace light profiles in general.

> Since you contributed code related to this exact matter I'm surprised by your criticism

It's not criticism, I want to understand how this PR is useful.

> this PR is basically just an extra elif that wasn't implemented at the time due to, I guess, simply not having encountered these somewhat weird bulbs

That's not the case, a light which supports colors can often approximate a white with a given color temperature with somewhat acceptable accuracy, but a light which supports white with adjustable color temperature will not be able to render any given color. Such a lights can only render a very very small part of the color space supported by a color light; the line in the xy-color space illustration below shows which of the colors in the xy-color space can be expressed as white with a given color temperatures: 
![image](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/assets/14281572/bc92b1ad-1f42-4c14-9623-bff2b027f878)

Bulbs with adjustable color temperatures are not at all weird, I'd say they are very common.

> The only actual behavioral change this code brings is that HA's default color presets will work as expected in terms of temperature, so users of temperature-only bulbs won't need to implement custom profiles and/or dedicated automations to replicate the states that are built into the stock apps for, let's say, my IKEA Tradfri bulbs that come with three temperature settings that can be toggled by the stock remote.

You're losing me here. I thought the rationale for this PR is precisely to allow users to add their own profiles and use those profiles  for white lights with adjustable color temperature? ~~The [example profiles which come with Home Assistant](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/master/homeassistant/components/light/light_profiles.csv) are not suitable, because they will set the lights to various, mostly red-ish, colors, and do not, at least not intentionally, replicate the presets of IKEA trådfri remotes.~~ I double checked, you're right about the example profiles, they actually lie on, or close to, the white line in the xy-color chart 👍 

Again, light profiles are very long overdue for a major overhaul, scenes are probably what you should use now.

issue_context.body:

## The problem
<!-- 
  Describe the issue you are experiencing here to communicate to the
  maintainers. Tell us what you were trying to do and what happened.
-->
Having recently installed IKEA TRADFRI light bulbs, I was looking at the `profile` setting in the `light.turn_on` service.
This setting allows you to call upon one of the predefined [light_profile's](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/master/homeassistant/components/light/light_profiles.csv) or to use a custom one.
The light profile makes use of the `xy_color` and `brightness` options.
However, IKEA TRADFRI bulbs do not respond to setting the `xy_color` option, resulting in only the `brightness` option having an effect.

I see 2 potential solutions here:

1. Map the xy-values to a `color_temp` value and (also) send this value when using a light_profile.
2. Add a column to the `light_profiles.csv` in which a `color_temp` value can be entered.

## Environment
<!--
  Provide details about the versions you are using, which helps us to reproduce
  and find the issue quicker. Version information is found in the
  Home Assistant frontend: Configuration -> Info.
-->

- Home Assistant Core release with the issue: 2021.1.1
- Last working Home Assistant Core release (if known): 
- Operating environment (OS/Container/Supervised/Core): Home Assistant OS
- Integration causing this issue: light
- Link to integration documentation on our website: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/light/

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`
<!--
  An example configuration that caused the problem for you. Fill this out even
  if it seems unimportant to you. Please be sure to remove personal information
  like passwords, private URLs and other credentials.
-->

```yaml
service: light.turn_on
data:
  entity_id: light.tradfri_bulb_level_light_color_on_off
  profile: reading
```

## Traceback/Error logs
<!--
  If you come across any trace or error logs, please provide them.
-->

```txt

```

## Additional information

The link to the [Hue Color Chart](https://developers.meethue.com/documentation/core-concepts#color_gets_more_complicated) mentioned at the `xy_color` option requires a Hue Developer account in order to be accessed.

review_comments:
Please add a comment which links to a source for this.
Wikipedia lists a cubic approximation credited to McCamy, but with slightly different coefficients: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Correlated_color_temperature#Approximation

Edit: FWIW this application note says the McCamy paper lists two set of coefficients: https://www.st.com/resource/en/application_note/an5638-how-correlated-color-temperature-is-calculated-by-vd6283-stmicroelectronics.pdf, the paper itself is locked behind paywall though.

My sources at the time were indeed the original paper and that STMicro's application note, but now my access to Wiley's library has expired so I can't check the fulltext. The [erratum](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/epdf/10.1002/col.5080180222) is publicly available though, and the constants roughly match - excluding the opposite signs which probably refer to some other step of the calculation.

I've tested all the three coefficients combinations I could find on the web (citing publications, StackOverflow, application notes) and they all give sufficiently similar results (or at least differ in amounts that aren't visible to the naked eye when rendered by a lightbulb), so I think it's pretty safe to link to the original paper.

Linking to STMicro's notes would be handy but I have no trust at all in that link staying up indefinitely, while at least the paper's DOI URL is pretty much guarateed to always resolve.
I've just added the link to the application note to the commit description though, so it's not completely lost in time.
